tiles.alt: BOOK TWO · THE FIRST WEEK / CHAPTER THIRTEEN / The Game
Sunday. / If you wanted to be specific, 9:48 on Sunday night.

The Great Hall at night: four long tables under the starry ceiling and floating candles; at the far end, Dumbledore rises at the podium. / The feast was over. The Sorting was over. The new Defence Professor had said his few words, and gone back to looking as though he might faint. / Dumbledore: Just a few more notices!

Dumbledore: First-years should note that the forest on the grounds is forbidden to all pupils. That is why it is called the Forbidden Forest. / Dumbledore: If it were permitted, it would be called the Permitted Forest.
Harry: Note to self: the Forbidden Forest is forbidden.
Under the table, Harry's hand has drifted to his pouch and come up holding a green can. / And for no reason at all, Harry felt a sudden, strong urge to drink a can of Comed-Tea.

Harry: Hey. I bet you're the same part of my brain that pushed through the prank on Neville Longbottom. / Harry: Er. Maybe? / Harry: And is it not overwhelmingly obvious that if I do this, I shall regret it one second after it is too late?
He puts the can away, very firmly. / Harry: Yeah. So, no.
Dumbledore: Quidditch trials will be held in the second week of term. Anyone interested in playing for their House teams should contact Madam Hooch.
Dumbledore: And anyone interested in reformulating the entire game of Quidditch should contact Harry Potter.
Harry chokes on nothing at all, spraying, as every head at the Ravenclaw table turns to stare. / KHHK! / Harry inhaled his own saliva.
Harry: How on Earth? He hadn't met Dumbledore's eyes at any point. He hadn't been thinking about Quidditch. He hadn't told anyone but Ron Weasley…
Dumbledore's eyes over his half-moon spectacles, twinkling, fixed on Harry. / Dumbledore was looking straight at him.
Dumbledore: Additionally, this year, the third-floor corridor on the right-hand side is out of bounds to everyone who does not wish to die a very painful death.
Harry was numb at this point.
Dumbledore: And now, before we go to bed, let us sing the school song! Everyone pick their favourite tune and favourite words, and off we go!
The whole Hall sings the school song, every student to a different tune; words in every style fly through the air.
Harry: Note to self: do not mess with Dumbledore.

The Ravenclaw first-years' dorm at night: five four-poster beds in blue and bronze. Boys argue in their pyjamas. Harry sits up in bed in the middle. / Anthony: It is NOT a theory if you can't test it! / Michael: Name one test! / There was a Quietus Charm on every headboard, with a little slider. It was the only reason it was ever possible for anyone to get to sleep in Ravenclaw.
Harry slides the brass slider on his headboard all the way up. The noise stops. / Click. / Silence.

The alarm clock on the nightstand: one o'clock, and the alarm hand set to seven. / Harry had tried to shift his twenty-six-hour day to fit Hogwarts. It was two minutes past one in the morning. / He set the alarm for seven. He'd have to ask Professor McGonagall about his sleep. Tomorrow.
Harry asleep. The candle out.
Monday. / If you wanted to be specific, 9:52 on Monday morning.
Harry's eyes, just opening. / It was quiet.
Too quiet.
The dorm: empty. / The beds: unmade. / The sun: rather high. / His Quieter: turned all the way up. / His alarm: switched off.
He'd missed breakfast. And his very first class at Hogwarts, Herbology, had started one hour and twenty-two minutes ago.

Frost creeps in at the edges as Harry's face goes flat and cold. / Harry: Oh, what a nice little prank. Turn off his alarm. Turn up the Quieter. Let Mr Bigshot Harry Potter miss his first class. / Harry: When Harry found out who'd done this…

The anger drains out of him, leaving a wounded look. / Harry: No. This could only have been done by all twelve of the other boys. All of them would have seen him asleep. All of them had let him sleep through breakfast. / Harry: They'd liked him. He'd thought.

A note pinned to his headboard, in pencil. / My fellow Ravenclaws,  It's been an extra long day. Please let me sleep in and don't worry about my missing breakfast. I haven't forgotten about my first class.  Harry Potter
Ice water in his veins. / It was in his own handwriting. In his own mechanical pencil. / And he didn't remember writing it.
Harry: Had he been Obliviated? Had he stayed up late, done something, and then… but he didn't know the spell… had someone else… / Harry: Wait. If he had known he was going to be Obliviated…
Still in his pyjamas, Harry has thumbed open his trunk and has his hand in the mokeskin pouch. / Harry: Note to myself.

The note from the pouch, in his own handwriting. / Dear Me,  Please play the game. You can only play the game once in a lifetime. This is an unrepeatable opportunity.  Recognition code 927, I am a potato.  You.

Memory: eight-year-old Harry on the floor in front of the television, pencil in hand, very serious. / "Recognition code 927, I am a potato" was a message he'd worked out years ago, in front of the television, that only he would ever know. In case he ever had to identify a duplicate of himself. Just in case. / Be Prepared.

On the back of the note, in perfectly regular writing: the instructions for The Game. / Instructions for The Game  you do not know the rules of the game  you do not know the stakes of the game  you do not know the objective of the game  you do not know who controls the game  you do not know how to end the game  You start with 100 points.  Begin.
He had absolutely no clue what was going on.
Well. Step one: eat. Luckily he'd visualised missing breakfast, and Prepared for it. / Harry: Snack bars.
Out of the pouch: two tiny chocolate bars, not nearly a meal, and a note. / Attempt failed: −1 point Current points: 99 Physical state: Still hungry Mental state: Confused
His mouth makes a noise without consulting him. / Harry: Gleehhhhh.
Harry, in pyjamas, alone in the sunny dorm, asks the empty air. / Harry: Ah… I don't suppose I could spend a point and get my box of cereal bars back? / There was only silence.
A box of cereal bars pops up: open, and completely empty. / Points spent: 1 Current points: 98 You have gained: A box of Cereal Bars
Harry: I'd like to spend one point and get the actual cereal bars back. / Nothing came out of the pouch. So he went to his cabinet to get dressed…

On the floor of the cabinet, under his robes: six cereal bars and another note. / Points spent: 1 Current points: 97 You have gained: 6 cereal bars You are still wearing: Pyjamas  Do not eat while you are wearing your pyjamas You will get a Pyjama Penalty
Harry: And now I know that whoever controls the game is insane.
Harry: My guess is that the game is controlled by Dumbledore. / Maybe this time he could set a new land speed record for being quick on the uptake.
But he was starting to see the pattern: the note would be in the next place he looked. So he looked under his bed.

Under the bed, a long note: laughter, "Dumbledore does not control the game", and a Pyjama Penalty. / Ha! Ha ha ha ha ha! Ha ha ha ha ha ha! Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha!  Dumbledore does not control the game  Bad guess  Very bad guess  −20 points  And you are still wearing pyjamas it is your fourth move and you are still wearing pyjamas  Pyjama penalty: −2 points Current points: 75
Harry: Welp. Once you ruled out Dumbledore, he didn't know the name of anyone else here who was this crazy.
Dressed at last, Harry paused before opening the drawer for his pyjamas. If the pattern held… / Harry: How can I earn more points?

In the drawer: the next note. / Opportunities to do good are everywhere but darkness is where the light needs to be  Cost of question: 1 point Current points: 74  Nice underwear Did your mother pick them out?
Harry crushed the note, face flaming scarlet. At this point he knew better than to say anything out loud. He'd probably get a Profanity Penalty.

Harry by the rubbish bin. In it, some red-and-green wrapping paper and a crumpled envelope. / He threw a wrapper in the bin (on top of a half-eaten Chocolate Frog, a crumpled envelope, and some red-and-green wrapping paper), and took one last look around for clues.
Harry: "Darkness is where the light needs to be." Down, then. The Slytherin dungeons.

The great stairwell: flights of stairs criss-crossing in every direction; the one Harry is on swings away beneath him. / Trying to navigate Hogwarts was like wandering around inside an Escher painting. Except that in an Escher painting, at least the stairs didn't move while you were still on them.

Out of the window, the clouds are below the castle. / After climbing down no fewer than twelve flights of stairs, Harry had concluded that he was somehow higher in the castle than when he'd started. / Harry: If I look out of the next window and see two moons, I will not even be surprised.
An empty corridor; a portrait of a wizened old lady in a lace cap. / Harry: I'm lost. Can, um, the spirit of the Hogwarts castle help me or something?
Lady: I don't think this castle has a spirit. Life, perhaps. But not spirit.
Harry: I'm Harry Potter. / Harry: Sorry. I'm sort of new here.
Lady: So I perceive, young raven. Where are you trying to go? / Harry: I'm not really sure. / Lady: Then perhaps you are already there.

Harry: Well, wherever I am trying to go, I don't think this is it… Okay, third try. I'm playing a game, I don't know the rules, I'm looking for opportunities to do good so I can score points, and all I have is this cryptic hint about how darkness is where the light needs to be, so I was trying to go down but I keep going up…
Harry: My life tends to get a bit peculiar.

Lady: Would it be fair to say that you don't know where you're going, or why you're trying to get there? / Harry: Entirely fair. / Lady: I'm not sure that being lost is your most important problem, young man.

Harry: True, but unlike the more important problems, it's a problem I can understand how to solve, and wow is this conversation turning into a metaphor for human existence, I didn't even realise that was happening until just now.
Lady: You are a fine young raven, aren't you? Well then. As a general rule, if you keep on turning left, you're bound to keep going down.
Harry: Um… have you heard of a mysterious game where you can only play once, and they won't tell you the rules? / Lady: Life. That's one of the most obvious riddles I've ever heard.

Harry: No. I mean an actual note, and somebody leaving me slips of paper about how many points I've lost, like a minus-two-point penalty for wearing pyjamas! Do you know anyone crazy enough and powerful enough to do that? Besides Dumbledore?

Lady: I'm only a picture, young man. I remember Hogwarts as it was, not Hogwarts as it is. / Lady: All I can tell you is that if this were a riddle, the answer would be that the game is life. And that while we do not make all the rules ourselves, the one who awards or takes points is always you.

Harry bows low to the painting; the painted lady curtseys back. / Harry: Thank you, milady. / Lady: I wish I could say I'll remember you with fondness. But I probably won't remember you at all. Farewell, Harry Potter.

A dead-end corridor, blocked by a cave-in. On the wall, a portrait of a man in dazzling pink. / Four left turns later, the corridor ended abruptly in a tumbled mound of rocks. / Harry: All right, I give up! I'm asking for another hint!

Flubberwalt: A hint! A hint, you say? / The portrait wore the loudest pink robes that Harry had ever seen or even imagined, and a droopy pointed hat with a fish on it. Not a drawing of a fish. A fish.

Flubberwalt: You're Harry Potter, aren't you? I'm Cornelion Flubberwalt! It was a message for me to give to you! No-one's cared about me in, I don't know how long, maybe ever! A hint! It will only cost you three points! Do you want it? / Harry: Yes! I want it!

Flubberwalt: The darkness can be found between the green study rooms and McGonagall's Transfiguration class! / Flubberwalt: And get a move on, you're slower than a sack of snails! Minus ten points for being slow! Now you have 61 points!

Harry: Um… I don't suppose you know where the message originally came from? / Flubberwalt: It was spoken by a hollow voice that belled forth from a gap within the air itself, a gap that opened upon a fiery abyss! That's what they told me!

Harry: Pencil and mechanical paper. Er, cancel that. Paper and mechanical pencil. / Flubberwalt: Spin round and go left, right, down, down, right, left, right, up, and left again! At least, that's how it was in my day. This is a Monday on an odd-numbered year, isn't it?

A lovely room lit green by stained-glass dragons. Harry has stopped dead at the bookshelf. / The green study room had comfortable chairs, and dragons in the stained glass, and sunlight coming through in green. Harry couldn't actually walk straight through it. / There were bookshelves. He had to read at least some of the titles, or lose his claim to the Verres family name.
A young boy's cry, from round the corner. / Voice: Please! Give them b-back!
Harry sprints.

A corridor: frightened Hufflepuffs on the left; five big Slytherin teenagers in a ring around a small boy whose books are scattered on the floor. / Six first-year Hufflepuffs, huddled together, looking as if they desperately wanted to do something. Five older Slytherins, in a ring around another boy.
Harry: EXCUSE ME!
Five older Slytherins turn to look down at him: anger, amusement, delight. / It might not have been necessary. People were already looking at him. But it certainly served to stop all the action cold.

Harry: Part of Harry's brain was screaming in panic that these were much older and bigger boys who could stomp him flat. / Harry: Another part said, dryly, that nobody would seriously stomp the Boy-Who-Lived with seven Hufflepuffs watching. Their only real weapon was his own fear. If he allowed it.
Neville Longbottom, tear-streaked, among the Slytherins' legs. / Then Harry saw who the boy was.
Harry: Of course. / Harry: He had decided to apologise to Neville. That meant Neville was his. How dare they?
Harry hauls Neville out of the ring so hard that Neville stumbles. / Harry grabbed Neville by the wrist and yanked him out, and in nearly the same motion pushed his own way into the gap.
Harry, small, stands in the middle of the ring of much bigger Slytherins, looking up at them. / Harry: Hello. / Harry: I'm the Boy-Who-Lived.
To be continued
